Join a "How to Apply" Webinar on the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) =
Grant Opportunity

Starting next week, the U.S. Department of Transportation will host three i=
nformational webinars on the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) competit=
ive grant program [ https://www.transportation.gov/grants/SS4A ]. The Fisca=
l Year (FY) 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity is now live [ https://www.tr=
ansportation.gov/grants/ss4a/fy26-nofo ] and open for applications.

All FY 2026 SS4A grant applications must be submitted by 5:00 PM (ET) on Tu=
esday, May 26, 2026.

These informational webinars will provide a general overview of the SS4A pr=
ogram and the grant application process, centered around individual emphasi=
s areas. Prospective SS4A applicants are encouraged to attend.

  SS4A [ https://www.transportation.gov/SS4A ]=20

________________________________________________________________________

=20

Webinar Dates and Registration

Webinar attendees must register in advance to attend each of the following =
sessions:

*Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Program - Implementation Grants*

"This webinar will offer a general overview of the SS4A program and the gra=
nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for Implementat=
ion Grants."

*Tuesday, April 7, 1:30 - 3:00 P.M. (ET)*

Register to attend the April 7 webinar [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar/=
register/WN_y65_q7y9TyiE9XITYMOc6w#/registration ].

* * *

*Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Program - Action Plans*

"This webinar will offer a general overview of the SS4A program and the gra=
nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for grants to d=
evelop an Action Plan."

*Thursday, April 9, 1:30 - 3:00 P.M. (ET)*

Register to attend the April 9 webinar [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar/=
register/WN_t4v5ugAFQGquobj16gX9rQ#/registration ].

* * *

*Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Program - Supplemental Planning and =
Demonstration Activities*

"This webinar will offer a general overview of the SS4A program and the gra=
nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for funding for=
 supplemental planning and demonstration activities."

*Tuesday, April 14, 1:30 - 3:00 P.M. (ET)*

Register to attend the April 14 webinar [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar=
/register/WN_pk6j2xchTjOHvkeDigOVUA#/registration ].

* * *

Please see the SS4A Webinar Series page [ https://www.transportation.gov/gr=
ants/SS4A/webinars ] for more details. For questions, please contact us at =
SS4A@dot.gov.

"About Safe Streets and Roads for All [ https://www.transportation.gov/SS4A=
 ]"

"Established by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the ""Safe Stre=
ets and Roads for All" [ https://www.transportation.gov/SS4A ]" (SS4A) comp=
etitive grant program will provide $5 billion in grant funding over five ye=
ars. Funding supports regional, local, and Tribal initiatives through grant=
s to prevent roadway deaths and serious injuries."

*HOLDING=C2=A0THE=C2=A0LINE: TRANSPORTATION'S DEFENSE AGAINST HUMAN TRAFFIC=
KING*

Join the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) for a webinar series to =
prepare transportation entities to prevent and address human trafficking in=
 advance of major sporting events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup=E2=84=
=A2. Transportation systems in host cities serve as the backbone of mobilit=
y during major sporting events, moving millions of spectators, workers, and=
 visitors. Increased travel, hospitality demands, and temporary workforces =
can heighten vulnerabilities to both labor and sex trafficking. Whether on =
roadways, railways, airways, or waterways, transportation entities are uniq=
uely positioned at points of transit, transfer, and arrival to report suspe=
cted human trafficking. These webinars will provide a practical readiness f=
ramework that strengthens leadership commitment, policy alignment, cross-se=
ctor partnerships, workforce preparedness, responsible data practices, and =
a survivor-informed response so transportation systems are prepared before =
kickoff and remain vigilant long after the final whistle.=C2=A0

Webinar Dates

  * *April 23, 2026 | 2:00 - 4:00pm EDT*=20
  * *April 30, 2026 | 2:00 - 4:00pm EDT*=20

*Who Should Attend*=C2=A0


  * State and local=C2=A0transportation=C2=A0authorities, operators,=C2=A0a=
nd=C2=A0industry associations=C2=A0=20
  * Transportation executives and senior leaders=C2=A0=20
  * Safety, security, and operations personnel=C2=A0=20
  * Event mobility planners=20

To move beyond awareness toward operational readiness, each=C2=A0webinar=C2=

lighting implementation insights from across the transportation sector. =C2=

As a result of this=C2=A0webinar, participants will have a better understan=
ding of:


  * The intersection of human trafficking with the transportation sector=C2=

for state, local,=C2=A0tribal, and private=C2=A0sector transportation entit=

<h2 style=3D"text-align: center; line-height: 1.2; font-family: helvetica; =
font-size: 18px; color: #333333; margin: 0 0 10px;" align=3D"center"><stron=
g><span class=3D"il">HOLDING</span>=C2=A0THE=C2=A0<span class=3D"il">LINE</=
span>: TRANSPORTATION'S DEFENSE AGAINST HUMAN TRAFFICKING</strong></h2>
<p align=3D"left" style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-ad=
just: 100%; line-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; colo=
r: #333333; text-align: left; margin: 0 0 15px;">Join the U.S. Department o=
f Transportation (USDOT) for a webinar series to prepare transportation ent=
ities to prevent and address human trafficking in advance of major sporting=
 events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup=E2=84=A2. Transportation systems=
 in host cities serve as the backbone of mobility during major sporting eve=
nts, moving millions of spectators, workers, and visitors. Increased travel=
, hospitality demands, and temporary workforces can heighten vulnerabilitie=
s to both labor and sex trafficking. Whether on roadways, railways, airways=
, or waterways, transportation entities are uniquely positioned at points o=
f transit, transfer, and arrival to report suspected human trafficking. The=
se webinars will provide a practical readiness framework that strengthens l=
eadership commitment, policy alignment, cross-sector partnerships, workforc=
e preparedness, responsible data practices, and a survivor-informed respons=
e so transportation systems are prepared before kickoff and remain vigilant=
 long after the final whistle.=C2=A0</p>
<h2 align=3D"left" style=3D"line-height: 1.2; font-family: helvetica; font-=
size: 18px; color: #333333; text-align: left; margin: 0 0 10px;">Webinar Da=
tes</h2>
<ul style=3D"margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 15px;">
<li style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; li=
ne-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; color: #333333; te=
xt-align: left; margin-top: 0px;"><strong>April 23, 2026 | 2:00 - 4:00pm ED=
T</strong></li>
<li style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; li=
ne-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; color: #333333; te=
xt-align: left; margin-bottom: 15px;"><strong>April 30, 2026 | 2:00 - 4:00p=
m EDT</strong></li>
</ul>
<p align=3D"left" style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-ad=
just: 100%; line-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; colo=
r: #333333; text-align: left; margin: 0 0 15px;"><strong>Who Should Attend<=
/strong>=C2=A0</p>
<ul style=3D"margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 15px;">
<li style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; li=
ne-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; color: #333333; te=
xt-align: left; margin-top: 0px;">State and local=C2=A0transportation=C2=A0=
<wbr></wbr>authorities, operators,=C2=A0and=C2=A0industry associations=C2=
=A0</li>
<li style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; li=
ne-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 13px; color: #333333; te=
xt-align: left;">Transportation executives and senior leaders=C2=A0</li>
<li style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; li=

"CORRECTION: The previous email sent at 11:45 a.m. ET contained an error re=
garding the year. Please note the application deadline for FY26 SS4A applic=
ations is May 26, _2026,_ at 5:00 p.m. ET"

=C2=A0

The Department of Transportation has released the fiscal year (FY) 2026 Not=
ice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Safe Streets and Roads for All (S=
S4A) [ https://www.transportation.gov/grants/SS4A ] program.

Established by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), the Safe =
Streets and Roads for All grant program funds regional, local, and Tribal i=
nitiatives through grants to prevent roadway deaths and serious injuries. A=
lmost $1 billion is made available by this NOFO.

=20

________________________________________________________________________

=20

Two Available Grant Types

The SS4A program provides funding for two main types of grants:=C2=A0=C2=A0


  * *Planning and Demonstration Grants* are used to develop, complete, or s=
upplement an Action Plan, as well as carry out demonstration activities tha=
t inform an Action Plan.=C2=A0=C2=A0=20

  * *Implementation Grants* are used to implement strategies or projects th=
at are consistent with an existing Action Plan and may also bundle funding =
requests for supplemental planning and demonstration activities that inform=
 the Action Plan.=20

________________________________________________________________________

=20

Applications and Deadline

The NOFO is posted on Grants.gov [ https://www.grants.gov/search-results-de=
tail/361291 ]; you may also view the NOFO on the SS4A Website [ https://www=
.transportation.gov/grants/ss4a/fy26-nofo ]. The deadline for applications =
is *May 26, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. (ET)*.=C2=A0

Applications must be submitted via Valid Eval, an online application portal=
 used by USDOT.=C2=A0


  * *Implementation Grant Application:* https://usg.valideval.com/teams/usd=
ot_ss4a_2026_implementation/signup=C2=A0=20

  * *Planning and Demonstration Grant Application:* https://usg.valideval.c=
om/teams/usdot_ss4a_2026_planning_demo/signup=C2=A0=20

Customer support for Valid Eval is available at support@valideval.com.

________________________________________________________________________

Register to attend the April 9 webinar [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar/=

<h2 style=3D"line-height: 1.2; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 22px; mar=
gin: 0.83em 0 18px;">Two Available Grant Types</h2>
<div>
<p style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; lin=
e-height: 1.4; font-family: helvetica; font-size: 15px; margin: 0 0 15px;">=
<span data-contrast=3D"auto" style=3D"line-height: 1.4;">The SS4A program p=
rovides funding for two main types of grants:=C2=A0</span><span data-ccp-pr=

U.S. Department of Transportation [ https://www.transportation.gov/SS4A ]
FY25 Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) NOFO Now Live!=20

Safe Streets and Roads for All logo [ https://www.transportation.gov/SS4A ]=
=20

The Department of Transportation has released the fiscal year (FY) 2026 Not=
ice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Safe Streets and Roads for All (S=
S4A) [ https://www.transportation.gov/grants/SS4A ] program.

Established by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), the Safe =
Streets and Roads for All grant program funds regional, local, and Tribal i=
nitiatives through grants to prevent roadway deaths and serious injuries. A=
lmost 1 billion is made available by this NOFO.

=20

________________________________________________________________________

=20

Two Available Grant Types

The SS4A program provides funding for two main types of grants:=C2=A0=C2=A0


  * *Planning and Demonstration Grants* are used to develop, complete, or s=
upplement an Action Plan, as well as carry out demonstration activities tha=
t inform an Action Plan.=C2=A0=C2=A0=20

  * *Implementation Grants* are used to implement strategies or projects th=
at are consistent with an existing Action Plan and may also bundle funding =
requests for supplemental planning and demonstration activities that inform=
 the Action Plan.=20

________________________________________________________________________

=20

Applications and Deadline

The NOFO is posted on Grants.gov; you may also view the NOFO on the SS4A We=
bsite [ https://www.transportation.gov/grants/ss4a/fy26-nofo ]. The deadlin=
e for applications is May 26, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. (ET).=C2=A0

Applications must be submitted via Valid Eval, an online application portal=
 used by USDOT.=C2=A0


  * *Implementation Grant Application:* https://usg.valideval.com/teams/usd=
ot_ss4a_2026_implementation/signup=C2=A0=20

  * *Planning and Demonstration Grant Application:* https://usg.valideval.c=
om/teams/usdot_ss4a_2026_planning_demo/signup=C2=A0=20

Customer support for Valid Eval is available at support@valideval.com.

________________________________________________________________________

=20

sessions:

nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for Implementat=
ion Grants."

register/WN_y65_q7y9TyiE9XITYMOc6w#/registration ].

* * *

*Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Program - Action Plans*

nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for grants to d=
evelop an Action Plan."

*Thursday, April 9, 1:30 - 3:00 P.M. (ET)*

Register to attend the April 9 webinar [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar/=
register/WN_t4v5ugAFQGquobj16gX9rQ#/registration ].

* * *

*Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) Program - Supplemental Planning and =
Demonstration Activities*

"This webinar will offer a general overview of the SS4A program and the gra=
nt application process, with a particular focus on applying for funding for=
 supplemental planning and demonstration activities."

*Tuesday, April 14, 1:30-3:00 P.M. (ET)*

 New protection measures

*HOLDING THE LINE: TRANSPORTATION'S DEFENSE AGAINST HUMAN TRAFFICKING*

Join the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) for=C2=A0a webinar=C2=A0=
series to prepare transportation entities to prevent and address human traf=
ficking in advance of the 2026 FIFA World Cup=E2=84=A2. Transportation syst=
ems in host cities will serve as the backbone of mobility during the event,=
 moving millions of spectators, workers, and visitors. Increased travel, ho=
spitality demands, and temporary workforces can heighten vulnerabilities to=
 both labor and sex trafficking. Whether on roadways, railways, airways, or=
 waterways, transportation entities are uniquely positioned at points of tr=
ansit, transfer, and arrival to report suspected human trafficking. These w=
ebinars will provide a practical readiness framework that strengthens leade=
rship commitment, policy alignment, cross-sector partnerships, workforce pr=
eparedness, responsible data practices, and a survivor-informed response so=
 transportation systems are prepared before kickoff and remain vigilant lon=
g after the final whistle.=C2=A0

Webinar Dates

  * *April 23, 2026 | 2:00 - 3:45pm EDT*=20
  * *April 30, 2026 | 2:00 - 3:45pm EDT*=20

*Who Should Attend*=C2=A0


  * State and local=C2=A0transportation=C2=A0authorities, operators,=C2=A0a=
nd=C2=A0industry associations=C2=A0=20
  * Transportation executives and senior leaders=C2=A0=20
  * Safety, security, and operations personnel=C2=A0=20
  * Event mobility planners=20

*_REGISTER HERE_* [ https://usdot.zoomgov.com/webinar/register/WN_BxOTIGLwT=
HaLl51QmW0EYg#/registration ]

To move beyond awareness toward operational readiness, each=C2=A0webinar=C2=
=A0will outline what meaningful preparedness looks like across modes. The=
=C2=A0webinar=C2=A0will also feature=C2=A0a=C2=A0multimodal panel=C2=A0high=
lighting implementation insights from across the transportation sector. =C2=
=A0

As a result of this=C2=A0webinar, participants will have a better understan=
ding of:


  * The intersection of human trafficking with the transportation sector=C2=
=A0=20
  * Indicators of sex and labor trafficking=C2=A0=20
  * A=C2=A0comprehensive approach to combating=C2=A0human trafficking=C2=A0=
for state, local,=C2=A0tribal, and private=C2=A0sector transportation entit=
ies=C2=A0=20
  * Relevant=C2=A0multimodal and mode-specific=C2=A0USDOT counter-trafficki=
ng resources=C2=A0=20
  * Examples=C2=A0of counter-trafficking best practices=C2=A0by operators=
=C2=A0in FIFA=E2=84=A2 host cities=C2=A0=20
=20
=20
=20
=20

=20
=20

ership statement, multimodal training, and public awareness materials.

urces-counter-human-trafficking-transportation-sector ]*

<p style=3D"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; lin=

f Transportation (USDOT) for=C2=A0a webinar=C2=A0series to prepare transpor=
tation entities to prevent and address human trafficking in advance of the =
2026 FIFA World Cup=E2=84=A2. Transportation systems in host cities will se=
rve as the backbone of mobility during the event, moving millions of specta=
tors, workers, and visitors. Increased travel, hospitality demands, and tem=
porary workforces can heighten vulnerabilities to both labor and sex traffi=
cking. Whether on roadways, railways, airways, or waterways, transportation=
 entities are uniquely positioned at points of transit, transfer, and arriv=
al to report suspected human trafficking. These webinars will provide a pra=
ctical readiness framework that strengthens leadership commitment, policy a=
lignment, cross-sector partnerships, workforce preparedness, responsible da=
ta practices, and a survivor-informed response so transportation systems ar=
e prepared before kickoff and remain vigilant long after the final whistle.=

ROUTES Initiative Request for Information (RFI)

________________________________________________________________________

=20

"The Rural Opportunities to Use Transportation for Economic Success (ROUTES=
 [ https://www.transportation.gov/rural ]) Initiative aims to address dispa=
rities in rural transportation infrastructure by disseminating resources on=
 its=C2=A0website [ https://www.transportation.gov/rural ]=C2=A0and providi=
ng technical assistance. If you want to learn more about ROUTES, or how it =
can help your community, you can reach the ROUTES team at=C2=A0rural@dot.go=
v."

=20

The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Rural Opportunities to Use Tran=
sportation for Economic Success (ROUTES) Initiative requests public input [=
 https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/02/23/2026-03496/rural-oppo=
rtunities-to-use-transportation-for-economic-success-initiative-request-for=
-information ] on unmet transportation infrastructure needs in rural commun=
ities, barriers that rural communities face in addressing those needs, and =
opportunities for ROUTES and the DOT to improve its services and technical =
assistance to support rural stakeholders and American families.=C2=A0

DOT specifically requests comments and data in response to the questions be=
low.=C2=A0


  * "Identifying=C2=A0Unmet Needs in Rural Transportation"=C2=A0=20
  * What challenges and opportunities do rural areas face related to the fo=
llowing:=20
  * infrastructure condition ("e.g.,"=C2=A0age of infrastructure or equipme=
nt, bridge closures or postings, weather resiliency);=C2=A0=20
  * usage ("e.g.,"=C2=A0frequency or availability of=C2=A0public transporta=
tion,=C2=A0freight=C2=A0transportation, pedestrian=C2=A0walkways=C2=A0and s=
houlders);=C2=A0=20
  * safety=C2=A0("e.g.," transportation-related injuries=C2=A0and=C2=A0fata=
lities,=C2=A0roadway departure,=C2=A0at-grade=C2=A0rail=C2=A0crossings,=C2=
=A0railroad trespassing,=C2=A0wildlife,=C2=A0transportation of hazardous ma=
terials,=C2=A0motorcycle and=C2=A0all-terrain vehicle=C2=A0safety,=C2=A0exp=
eriences of nonmotorized road users,=C2=A0post-crash care);=C2=A0=20
  * technology ("e.g.,"=C2=A0broadband,=C2=A0cellular coverage,=C2=A0backup=
 for GPS time and navigation, automated vehicles,=C2=A0drones, digital infr=
astructure);=C2=A0=20

  * What types of infrastructure projects,=C2=A0services, or technology=C2=
=A0are most needed in rural communities to meet national transportation pri=
orities such as safety and economic competitiveness?=C2=A0What types of pro=
jects or services do rural=C2=A0communities find most challenging to fund?=
=C2=A0What are barriers to funding these projects?=C2=A0=20
  * How=C2=A0could=C2=A0improved=C2=A0multimodal=C2=A0passenger and freight=
=C2=A0transportation=E2=80=94including=C2=A0road, rail, transit, aviation, =
maritime, pipelines, and other forms of transportation=E2=80=94better contr=
ibute to the economic competitiveness of rural communities?=C2=A0What indus=
tries (including tourism) are=C2=A0most in need of=C2=A0these improvements?=
=C2=A0=20
  * What data has been used to inform rural transportation decision making =
and grant development, and what=C2=A0additional=C2=A0data would have been h=
elpful but was nonexistent or=C2=A0difficult=C2=A0to access?=C2=A0=C2=A0=C2=
=A0=20
  * How can rural communities better engage with Federal, Tribal, State, an=
d regional entities=E2=80=94such as other Federal agencies, State DOTs, reg=
ional planning organizations, and metropolitan planning organizations=E2=80=
=94to maintain and upgrade local transportation?=20

  * =C2=A0"Addressing Unmet Needs=C2=A0Through DOT=C2=A0Grants=C2=A0and=C2=
=A0Resources"=C2=A0=20
  * ROUTES=C2=A0supports rural and Tribal stakeholders through development =
of technical assistance=C2=A0resources=C2=A0and opportunities, such as tool=
kits,=C2=A0dashboards,=C2=A0peer exchanges, webinars,=C2=A0and=C2=A0newslet=
ters.=C2=A0(See=C2=A0https://www.transportation.gov/rural=C2=A0for more inf=
ormation on ROUTES activities.)=C2=A0What=C2=A0additional=C2=A0resources=C2=
=A0or direct technical assistance=C2=A0could=C2=A0ROUTES=C2=A0provide to su=
pport rural=C2=A0communities?=C2=A0Of the existing resources=C2=A0ROUTES pr=
ovides, what=C2=A0is most useful?=C2=A0=20
  * What challenges do rural communities face when applying for DOT grants=
=C2=A0and financial=C2=A0assistance=C2=A0("e.g.,"=C2=A0project prioritizati=
on, eligibility requirements, data needs, funding match)?=C2=A0What challen=
ges do rural communities encounter=C2=A0after being awarded a DOT grant=C2=
=A0or=C2=A0financial=C2=A0assistance=C2=A0("e.g.,"=C2=A0project grant=C2=A0=
agreements, environmental analyses,=C2=A0permitting,=C2=A0reporting require=
ments,=C2=A0workforce availability,=C2=A0weather,=C2=A0inflation)?=C2=A0=20
  * What types=C2=A0of technical=C2=A0assistance=C2=A0would be effective fo=
r navigating the Federal grant process, including=C2=A0pre-award=C2=A0activ=
ities,=C2=A0project delivery, and project evaluation?=C2=A0=20
  * How do the definitions of =E2=80=9Crural=E2=80=9D across DOT grant prog=
rams11 reflect the reality of rural communities? How do these definitions i=
nfluence the allocation of rural funding?=20

Comments must be received on or before April 24, 2026 at 11:59PM EDT. DOT w=
ill consider comments filed after this date to the extent practicable.=C2=A0

For further information, visit http://www.transportation.gov/rural, or cont=
act the ROUTES Office at rural@dot.gov.

The Embassy of Sweden migration section has received your email. If the ans=
wer to your query can be found below you will not receive an individual rep=
ly from the Embassy. You are therefore requested to read the below informat=
ion thoroughly. Our aim is to respond to emails within three working days. =
All emails are handled in the order they are received by the Embassy.

The Migration section=92s opening- and telephone hours can be found on our =
website:  Contact - Sweden Abroad<https://www.swedenabroad.se/en/embassies/=
india-new-delhi/contact/>. The Embassy=92s main switchboard does not handle=
 migration cases and cannot transfer your call to the migration section.

Applicants are not required to schedule an appointment for;

  *   biometric submission and passport check (will only be done if request=
ed by migration agency) for residence permits or;
  *   collection of residence permit cards and decision letters.


More information regarding passport checks and biometrics can be found on o=
ur website: Biometrics and passport checks - Sweden Abroad<https://www.swed=
enabroad.se/en/about-sweden-non-swedish-citizens/india/going-to-sweden/biom=
etrics-and-passport-checks/>.

Applicant must schedule an appointment via email<mailto:migration.new-delhi=
@gov.se>;

  *   to hand in an application for a residence permit,
  *   to hand in an application for a national visa (D visa) or;
  *   when you have received an interview request in your case from the Swe=
dish Migration Agency.


Please note that applicants are required to carry their original passports =
during their visit at the Embassy.

e: Going to Sweden? - Sweden Abroad<https://www.swedenabroad.se/en/about-sw=

lcome to VFS Global | vfsglobal<https://visa.vfsglobal.com/ind/en/swe/>

onsverket.se/English/Private-individuals/Working-in-Sweden.html>

cy=92s website: Studying in Sweden - Migrationsverket<https://www.migration=
sverket.se/English/Private-individuals/Studying-in-Sweden.html>

The Embassy will not reply to any questions about expected delivery of resi=
dence permit cards. Once the card has reached the Embassy, you will receive=
 an auto-generated e-mail on your registered email.

The Embassy is a government authority. Messages sent to the Embassy become =
official documents and may be disclosed under the principle of public acces=
s to official documents.

The Embassy processes personal data in connection with various types of mat=
ters. Personal data that is not part of an official document is only saved =
as long as necessary for the purposes for which it is processed, and then d=
eleted or pseudonymized on a regular basis in accordance with the EU=92s Ge=
neral Data Protection Regulation. The Embassy has the same routines regardi=

Hello Francisco,

Thank you for your email, it's great to hear that you're interested in our =
BA (Hons) Business & Management course<https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/study/=
courses/ba-hons-business-management-2>,

The general entry requirements for this course are a minimum of 104 UCAS po=
ints. You can use the UCAS calculator<https://www.ucas.com/applying/before-=
you-apply/what-and-where-to-study/entry-requirements/calculate-your-ucas-ta=
riff-points> to see how your qualifications equate to UCAS tariff points.
The tuition fees for this degree can be found on the course page linked abo=
ve.

For our international applicants, you can view the specific entry requireme=
nts for your country<https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/study/international/bu-y=
our-country> on this webpage. If English is not your first language, you wi=
ll need to provide evidence that you can understand English to a satisfacto=
ry level. English language requirements for this course for September 2026 =
entry are: IELTS (Academic) 6.0 with a minimum of 5.5 in each component, or=
 equivalent<https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/study/international/preparatory-p=
rogrammes/english-language-requirements/english-language-comparison-scores>=
. You can view further information about our English language requirements<=
https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk/study/international/preparatory-programmes/en=
glish-language-requirements>.

We also have an online scholarship calculator<https://www.bournemouth.ac.uk=
/scholarships> which you can use to determine which of our scholarships you=
 may be eligible for and the application process.

I hope this helps! Let us know if you have any more questions.

Rachel Pilley (she/her)

=F0=9F=94=B9 Registering as a New Patient

To get started, you will need to:

   1.

   2.

   Complete the online registration form.
   3.

   Upload any relevant medical records (if available).
   4.

   Book and pay for your initial consultation.

Our team will review your information and confirm your appointment once
everything has been submitted.
=F0=9F=94=B9 Appointment Availability

We currently have appointments available within the next 7=E2=80=9310 days,

=F0=9F=94=B9 Consultation Fees

We offer two pathways:

*Pay As You Go*

   -

   =C2=A369.00 =E2=80=93 Initial consultation
   -

   =C2=A39.99 =E2=80=93 Repeat prescription (as needed)
   -

   =C2=A349.99 =E2=80=93 6-month follow-up consultation

*Monthly Subscription*

   -

   =C2=A311.90 per month (minimum 12-month commitment)
   -

   Includes free consultations, repeat prescriptions, delivery from partner
   pharmacies, and additional services.

GP referral is required; however, medical records are helpful for
assessment purposes.
=F0=9F=94=B9 Virtual Appointments

Yes, all consultations are conducted remotely via secure video
consultation, so you can attend from home.
=F0=9F=94=B9 Required Documents

Before your consultation, we recommend preparing:

   -

   A form of photo ID
   -

   Proof of address
   -

   Relevant medical history or summary care record (if available)

 offer, please upload these to your Applicant Portal<https://evision.prod.g=
cu.tribalsits.com/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn>.

For guidance on suitable documents please see our Supporting Documents guid=
ance<https://www.gcu.ac.uk/london/study/applications-and-enquiries/supporti=
ng-documents>.

Problems with your Applicant Portal

If you are having issues logging into your Applicant Portal use the Forgott=
en Password button found on the Applicant Portal<https://evision.prod.gcu.t=
ribalsits.com/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn>. Once following the Forgotten Passw=
ord link and providing the required information, please make sure to check =
your Junk or Spam folder for any GCU emails. The email link to reset your p=
assword can take 8 hours to arrive after being requested. Please do not req=
uest a second password reset within that time frame.

Please note, your account will lock after six unsuccessful login attempts i=
n a day, but will unlock at midnight. Once an account is locked, a password=
 reset during this time will not unlock it.

roviding technical assistance. If you want to learn more about ROUTES, or h=
ow it can help your community, visit the ""ROUTES Initiative" [ https://www=

USDOT Funding & Financing

USDOT Announces $1.5 Billion in Infrastructure Funding to Get America Build=
ing Again [ https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/trumps-transportat=
ion-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-15-billion-infrastructure ]

The U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) has announced a Notice of Fun=
ding Opportunity (NOFO) [ https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/3609=
21 ]=C2=A0through Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUI=
LD) Grants for Fiscal Year 2026 that makes $1.5 billion available for infra=
structure projects across the country. =C2=A0

Under Secretary Duffy, the merit criteria of BUILD grants will prioritize i=
ncreasing safety measures, expanding transportation options for American fa=
milies, as well as projects that: =C2=A0


  * Beautify transportation infrastructure with context-appropriate design =
that enhance user experience while maintaining safety and operational effic=
iency;=C2=A0=20
  * Improve roadway capacity and makes transportation more affordable;=C2=
=A0=20
  * Improve the travel experience for families through dedicated facilities=
 for mothers, accessibility for those with disabilities, intuitive design e=
lements, clear signage, intuitive layouts, and predictable operations for c=
aregivers;=C2=A0=20
  * Facilitate tourism;=C2=A0=20
  * Support U.S. energy dominance.=C2=A0=20

_*Additional Information:=C2=A0*_

The program=E2=80=99s goal is to identify transportation projects with the =
capacity to have significant local or regional impacts, including highway, =
rail, port, and truck parking projects. BUILD grants are awarded on a compe=
titive basis for planning or constructing surface transportation infrastruc=
ture projects that will improve safety; quality of life; mobility and commu=
nity connectivity; economic competitiveness and opportunity including touri=
sm; state of good repair; partnership and collaboration; and innovation.=C2=
=A0

Applications [ https://www.transportation.gov/BUILDgrants/apply ]=C2=A0are =
due February 24, 2026, at 5:00 pm eastern.

FTA Invests $2 Billion in Modernizing America's Transit Bus Infrastructure =
[ https://www.transit.dot.gov/about/news/trumps-transportation-secretary-se=
an-p-duffy-invests-2-billion-modernizing-americas ]=C2=A0=20

The Federal Transit Administration (FTA) has announced an investment of $2 =
billion in 165 transit projects in 45 States and Washington, D.C. The funds=
 will deliver 2,400 buses built with American parts and labor=E2=80=94a pro=
ud example of President Trump's America First agenda.=C2=A0

Funding from the Grants for Buses and Bus Facilities Program [ https://www.=
transit.dot.gov/bus-program ]=C2=A0and the=C2=A0Low or No Emission Grant Pr=
ogram [ https://www.transit.dot.gov/lowno ]=C2=A0will help modernize Americ=
a's bus infrastructure, reduce traffic congestion, and help people travel m=
ore efficiently and affordably. These competitive grants will also create g=
ood-paying jobs in both rural and urban communities across the country. A f=
ull breakdown of the project selections is available=C2=A0here [ https://ww=
w.transit.dot.gov/funding/grants/fy25-fta-bus-and-low-and-no-emission-grant=
-awards ]. In addition, through advance appropriations, FTA is adding $518 =
million in fiscal year (FY) 2026 funding through the Low or No Emission Pro=
gram to make additional selections.=C2=A0

FHWA Announces Availability of Over $40 Million to Improve Roadway Safety o=
n Tribal Lands and Get America Building Again [ https://highways.dot.gov/ne=
wsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-availability-=
over-40-million ]=C2=A0=20

The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) has announced over $40 million in=
 available funding to help Tribal governments improve roadways and address =
transportation safety issues through the Tribal Transportation Program Safe=
ty Fund (TTPSF) [ https://highways.dot.gov/federal-lands/tribal/safety/fund=
s ]. This announcement will help eligible applicants =E2=80=93 the 574 Fede=
rally recognized Tribes =E2=80=93 meet their transportation infrastructure =
priorities and help reduce the risk of serious roadway departures and fatal=
 crashes, particularly for those living and working in Native American and =
Alaska Native communities. Project improvements may include measures that k=
eep drivers in their lanes, enable safe recovery along roadsides, and strat=
egies that reduce the severity of accidents. You can read the amended NOFO =
here [ https://highways.dot.gov/federal-lands/tribal/safety/funds/TTPSF_NOF=
O_Amendment_2_for_publication_clean.pdf ].=C2=A0

USDOT Announces Nearly $500 Million in Funding to Revitalize American Infra=
structure [ https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/president-trumps-t=
ransportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-nearly-500-million ]

The USDOT has announced $488 million in awards from the Better Utilizing In=
vestments to Leverage Development [ https://www.transportation.gov/BUILDgra=
nts ] (BUILD) grant program for 30 projects across the country. The funding=
 will support critical roadway, transit, rail, maritime, and aviation infra=
structure improvements that improve safety, reduce congestion, and spur eco=
nomic growth.=C2=A0

Key Facts:=C2=A0


  * Roads and bridges received 77% of the funding from this grant series to=
 reinforce the arteries of the American economy.=C2=A0=20
  * Ex: Over $24 million to widen an approximately 14-mile segment of US Ro=
ute 54 from a two-lane roadway to a shared four-lane configuration between =
Farber and Curryville, Missouri.=C2=A0=20

  * 10% of the grants are being awarded to transit upgrades to deliver safe=
, reliable, and accessible commuter networks.=C2=A0=20
  * Waterway projects received more than $35 million primarily for port imp=
rovements to enhance American maritime dominance.=C2=A0=20
  * Nearly $3 million will support rail networks to enhance multimodal surf=
ace transportation.=C2=A0=20
  * The West Virginia Division of Highways (WVDOH) will receive roughly $25=
 million towards expanding trucking parking in Cabell, Monongalia, and Berk=
eley Counties along I-81, I-64, and I-79.=20

The full list of projects can be viewed here. [ https://www.transportation.=
gov/BUILDgrants/awarded-projects ]=C2=A0

Research & Technology

Traffic Crash Deaths | Early Estimates Jan-June 2025 [ https://www.nhtsa.go=
v/press-releases/nhtsa-reports-sharp-drop-traffic-fatalities-first-half-202=
5 ]=C2=A0=20

NHTSA has released early estimates for motor vehicle traffic fatalities in =
the first half of 2025 [ https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPu=
blication/813756 ], projecting a substantial 8.2% decline in roadway deaths=
. An estimated 17,140 people lost their lives in motor vehicle crashes from=
 January through June 2025, down from 18,680 fatalities during the same per=
iod in 2024.=C2=A0=C2=A0

The decline in fatalities occurred even as vehicle miles traveled increased=
 by 12.1 billion miles during the first half of 2025. As a result, the fata=
lity rate per 100 million vehicle miles traveled dropped to 1.06, down 8.6%=
 from 1.16 in the same period last year. This represents the lowest mid-yea=
r fatality rate since 2014.=C2=A0=C2=A0

Additionally, 38 States, along with the District of Columbia and Puerto Ric=
o, are projected to have experienced decreases in traffic deaths. Only 11 S=
tates are projected to see increases, while one State remains unchanged.=C2=
=A0

Round Up

Top Transportation Officials Underscore USDOT=E2=80=99s Commitment to Safet=
y on Roads for First Responders and Partnership with State DOTs at AASHTO A=
nnual Meeting [ https://highways.dot.gov/newsroom/must-read-top-trump-trans=
portation-officials-underscore-usdots-commitment-safety-roads ]=C2=A0=20

The Federal Highway Administrator, Sean McMaster, highlighted the U.S. Depa=
rtment of Transportation=E2=80=99s latest actions to improve safety on the =
nation=E2=80=99s highways, roads and bridges, including efforts to make tra=
ffic incident management safer for first responders, as well as the agency=
=E2=80=99s ongoing work with its State DOT partners to make travel safer fo=
r all road users. =C2=A0

On November 14, the FHWA announced [ https://highways.dot.gov/newsroom/trum=
ps-transportation-secretary-duffy-secures-nationwide-support-life-saving-sa=
fe-roads-initiative ] that U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy has =
secured nationwide participation from all State partners for the agency=E2=
=80=99s Safe Arterials for Everyone through Reliable Operations and Distrac=
tion-Reducing Strategies (SAFE ROADS) initiative. Launched to reduce roadwa=
y fatalities, SAFE ROADS emphasizes the administration=E2=80=99s effort to =
get back to basics and address safety on non-freeway arterials, where more =
than half of all U.S. roadway deaths occurred in 2023.=C2=A0

On November 20, Administrator McMaster spoke at the American Association of=
 State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) Annual Board of Direct=
ors Meeting in Salt Lake City, UT and commended State DOTs for their hard w=
ork on the SAFE ROADS initiative. Looking to the future, McMaster stated th=
at FHWA wants to give more flexibility to State and local governments and g=
et back to basics by building big, beautiful bridges and roads, since State=
 DOTs and local agencies understand their transportation needs best.=C2=A0

=C2=A0

FMCSA Launches New Initiatives to Improve Trucker=E2=80=99s Quality of Life=
 on the Road [ https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-sec=
retary-sean-p-duffy-launches-new-initiatives-improve-truckers ] =C2=A0

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) has announced the l=
aunch of two bold new pilot programs aimed at improving the working conditi=
ons and quality of life for America=E2=80=99s truck drivers. The FMCSA will=
 study increased flexibility in the current hours-of-service (HOS) regulati=
ons, which will help determine if providing drivers with greater control ov=
er their own schedule will reduce fatigue and improve safety.=C2=A0=C2=A0 =
=C2=A0


  * *Split Duty Period pilot program: *This will allow participating driver=
s to pause their 14-hour =E2=80=9Cdriving window=E2=80=9D for no less than =
30 minutes and no more than three hours. The program seeks to collect data =
and assess whether added flexibility can maintain or improve safety outcome=
s.=C2=A0=C2=A0=20
  * *Flexible Sleeper Berth pilot program*: This will explore additional sl=
eeper berth split options beyond the current =E2=80=9C8/2=E2=80=9D and =E2=
=80=9C7/3=E2=80=9D configurations. FMCSA will test the safety implications =
of allowing drivers to divide their 10-hour off-duty requirement into =E2=
=80=9C6/4=E2=80=9D and =E2=80=9C5/5=E2=80=9D split periods. The research wi=
ll examine how these alternatives affect driver fatigue and overall safety =
performance in order to determine whether a wider range of rest options cou=
ld benefit both drivers and the motoring public.=C2=A0=20

*Additional Information:*=C2=A0

The pilot programs are part of the Department=E2=80=99s Pro-Trucker Package=
 [ https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/us-transportation-secretary=
-sean-p-duffy-unveils-pro-trucker-package-part-president ], unveiled in Jun=
e by Secretary Duffy in support of President Trump=E2=80=99s Executive Orde=
r 14286 [ https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/enforcing=
-commonsense-rules-of-the-road-for-americas-truck-drivers/ ], Enforcing Com=
monsense Rules of the Road for America=E2=80=99s Truck Drivers. The wide-ra=
nging package includes millions of dollars in investments for expanded truc=
k parking, modernized driver resources, commonsense regulatory reforms to e=
liminate one-size-fits-all mandates, and efforts to crack down on bad actor=
s.=C2=A0=C2=A0=C2=A0

Register notices [ https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2025-1=
7938/hours-of-service-of-drivers-pilot-program-to-allow-commercial-drivers-=
to-pause-their-14-hour-driving ] for both the Split Duty Period pilot progr=
am and the Flexible Sleeper Berth pilot program are available for review. T=
he notices invite public comment and provide additional details. FMCSA will=
 carefully review all submissions. Protocol development for both pilot prog=
rams will begin in early 2026, with more than 500 commercial truck drivers =
expected to participate in the efforts.=C2=A0

USDOT Kicks Off Surface Transportation Reauthorization to Get America Build=
ing Again [ https://highways.dot.gov/newsroom/us-transportation-secretary-s=
ean-p-duffy-kicks-off-surface-transportation-reauthorization ]=C2=A0=20

The U.S. Department of Transportation brought together Congressional member=
s and infrastructure stakeholders in a first-of-its-kind conference to fost=
er collaboration on priorities ahead of Congress=E2=80=99s surface transpor=
tation reauthorization process later this year.=C2=A0

During his remarks [ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3D0QQ2XbiuA3M&t=3D2s ]=
, Secretary Duffy outlined the America is Building Again agenda, including:=
=C2=A0


  * *Enhancing transportation safety, *including bridges, safety for transp=
ortation workers and pedestrians, truck parking, and autonomous vehicles.=
=C2=A0=20
  * *Accelerating project delivery* for transportation projects, including =
reforming the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and permitting, enha=
ncing One Federal Decision, and increasing the use of technology.=C2=A0=20
  * *Increasing opportunities* through investment in transportation infrast=
ructure that promotes economic growth, including through expanded capacity =
and mobility, congestion relief, and more private sector investment.=C2=A0 =

  * *Strengthening partnerships* with States and other key stakeholders to =
improve transportation outcomes, including prioritizing the Federal interes=
t, greater efficiencies, and research.=C2=A0=20
